_readme: The Community Service Project as the mentor-verified report records it (GPREC, CSE-AIML, 4 May to 20 June 2026). Dates, weeks, themes, the five gaps found, the rules taught and the SDG mapping come from that report. The report holds findings, not survey counts, so no percentage or head-count appears here or on the site. The About page numbers are computed from this file; scripts/campaign_regions.js refuses a file whose weeks do not join up.
title: FraudShield - A Simulation-Based Digital Fraud Immunity System

weeks.title: Plan it like a campaign
weeks.did: Researched the frauds hurting people most: phishing, OTP, UPI, QR and digital arrest. Wrote a questionnaire that collects no personal data. Printed the safety checklists. Fixed the eight-week plan.

weeks.title: Go out and listen first
weeks.did: First visits. Put the questionnaire in people's hands, asked how they pay and what they use, then analysed the answers. The gaps were phishing links, OTP sharing and fake payment methods.

weeks.title: Call the scam by its name
weeks.did: First awareness sessions. Phishing, smishing and vishing in plain words, with real examples, and the warning signs: urgency, odd links, spelling errors, unknown senders.

weeks.title: Think before you share
weeks.did: How scammers stitch your public details into an attack. Then deepfakes and voice cloning: seeing is no longer believing. A hands-on check of what each person's own online presence gives away.

weeks.title: Four rules people can remember
weeks.did: Stop and think. Keep it secret. Don't accept. Use strong passwords. Practised with two-factor authentication and real fake-support-call examples.

weeks.title: What to do after it happens
weeks.did: Don't panic. Don't delete. Tell the bank or platform. Call 1930 and report at cybercrime.gov.in. Practised until people stopped being afraid to report.

weeks.title: Make them the teachers
weeks.did: The Digital Defender idea: the people who learned it teach their neighbours. App permissions, privacy settings, and a session where the community shared the rules themselves.

weeks.title: Measure it, then hand it over
weeks.did: Post-campaign assessment, a review meeting with community representatives, and the full report written to the college's guidelines.

gaps.title: Weak passwords
gaps.saw: Easy passwords, one password everywhere, logins shared with staff and family for convenience.
gaps.did: Strong, unique passwords, never shared, with two-factor authentication switched on.

gaps.title: Payment scams
gaps.saw: Fake payment messages, fake support calls, QR scams and cashback links that lean on urgency.
gaps.did: A zero-trust rule: any unexpected OTP, bank detail or payment request is suspect until verified.

gaps.title: Oversharing
gaps.saw: Shop names, phone numbers, payment QR codes and locations posted where anyone can collect them.
gaps.did: Protect your private information, and audit what you have already put out.

gaps.title: Afraid to report
gaps.saw: People unsure what to do, scared of losing face or money, deleting the very messages police need.
gaps.did: A calm four-step response, and the official channels: 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in.

gaps.title: AI scams unseen
gaps.saw: Hard to tell a real message from a fake. Deepfakes and cloned voices were new to most people.
gaps.did: Stop and verify before you answer, whoever it sounds like.

golden.name: Stop and think
golden.line: Pause before you answer any unknown link, message or request.

golden.name: Keep it secret
golden.line: Passwords and OTPs are never shared with anyone.

golden.name: Don't accept
golden.line: Unknown contacts, odd messages and unverified requests get declined.

golden.name: Use strong passwords
golden.line: Letters, numbers and symbols. Nothing guessable.

response.name: Don't panic
response.line: It can happen to anyone, including careful people.

response.name: Don't delete
response.line: Keep the messages, the transaction details and the link. They are evidence.

response.name: Tell them fast
response.line: Inform your bank or the platform and change the passwords.
